sborindex.name: SBOR · Standard Bitcoin Offered Rate
sborindex.bio: The daily reference rate for borrowing dollars against bitcoin. Read from lending contracts, posted on-chain. Free to read, built for agents.
texts: Before an agent borrows, it can ask one question: is this rate fair? SBOR's MCP server answers with the gap to the market rate in basis points, and tells the agent to stop when an offer is more than 50 bps above it. Free, no key, no sign-up.

After each daily fixing, SBOR posts the day's rates to contracts on Stacks, Arc, Base, Hyperliquid and Solana. Any app, vault or agent can read them on-chain, and anyone can check a past day against what was posted that day. https://sbor.xyz/?v=3

Your agent is borrowing blind. Thursday, November 5, 6 PM ET: a 45 minute @BFFARMY_ session. Connect an agent to SBOR and it checks any loan offer against the market rate before it borrows. Free. No key, no signup, no wallet. https://x.com/BFFARMY_/status/2115518042562072816

A benchmark that always has an answer is sometimes guessing. When SBOR can't read enough of a rate's markets, it withholds the rate and says why. A missing number means unknown, never zero. The rules behind every fixing: https://sbor.xyz/paper.html

60 days of SBOR. A fixing every morning since September 1, none missed, weekends included. Every one read from the lending contracts, every market shown, never rewritten. A benchmark is earned one fixing at a time. https://sbor.xyz/?v=3

Borrowing dollars against bitcoin cost 5.45% in this morning's fixing, down from 6.00% a day earlier. The largest market, USDC against cbBTC on Morpho on Base, went from 6.26% to 5.71%. Every market behind it at https://sbor.xyz/?v=3

5% and 5% are not always the same rate. Protocols quote on different bases, and a nominal 5% compounded continuously costs 5.13% over a year. SBOR converts each market's rate to one effective annual basis before it averages them. https://sbor.xyz

Borrowing dollars against bitcoin cost 6.00% in this morning's fixing, up from 5.10% a day earlier. The largest market, USDC against cbBTC on Morpho on Base, went from 5.30% to 6.26%. Every market behind it at SBOR.

The SBOR white paper is out. What a reference rate for loans against bitcoin must be, how SBOR computes it, and what changes when lenders and borrowers use the same rate. Stamped on Bitcoin, Arc, Base, Hyperliquid, Solana and Stacks. https://sbor.xyz/whitepaper

Check it yourself. The PDF's SHA-256 is eb87f320b33ff590a6bab498167ee2d192525f7c3edc28604a2af13a66cfe638, posted on all six chains on 25 October. The page checks the file in your browser and links every transaction.

Every lending pool has two prices: what borrowers pay and what lenders earn. Lenders earn less, because only part of the pool is lent out and the protocol keeps a share. That is why SBOR publishes two rates, a borrow rate and a supply rate, every day. https://sbor.xyz

What a dollar costs, 21 Oct. Rate, then utilization. Stacks, SBOR-USD, against crypto collateral: 2.83%, 56.92% Against plain bitcoin, BTC-COLLATERAL-USD, 19 markets on 5 chains: 5.08%, 89.71% Against US Treasuries, SOFR (19 Oct): 3.87%

An app shows you a rate. The lending contract is what charges it. SBOR reads its rates from the contracts' own state every morning, and lists every market behind each number on the site, so anyone can check the source. https://sbor.xyz
SBOR-BTC, 20 Oct fixing: borrow 1.50%, supply 1.34%. 19 Oct: 1.30% and 0.81%. Its one market, sBTC on Zest, went from 70.62% to 99.97% utilization over the same two fixings.
First stablecoin sub-rate: borrowing RLUSD against bitcoin costs 3.70% today (BTC-COLLATERAL-RLUSD), beside 5.06% for USDC. One rate per stablecoin once $25M of it is weighted in.
PoX cycle 144 paid 7.859 BTC to STX stakers, up 58.9% on cycle 143, with 448.3M STX locked, up 1.5%. Every cycle, read from the chain, formula shown: https://sbor.xyz

What does it cost to borrow dollars against bitcoin? SBOR reads the lending contracts every morning and publishes one dated rate. 16 October: 5.10% to borrow, across 20 markets on 6 chains and $3.1B supplied. Every market behind it is shown. https://sbor.xyz
The same bitcoin, borrowed in different dollars. 16 October: 5.23% in USDC on Base, 2.99% in USDT on Ethereum, 1.79% in USD1 on BNB Chain. One reference rate puts them side by side.

Built for AI agents. Before your agent borrows, it can check the offer against SBOR. Free MCP server, no key: npx -y sbor-mcp. Each day’s rate is also posted on-chain on Arc, Base, Hyperliquid, Solana and Stacks.

Is 6% a good rate to borrow dollars against bitcoin? Alone, a rate tells you nothing. Credit markets judge offers against a published market rate, like SOFR for dollars borrowed against Treasuries. SBOR publishes one for dollars borrowed against bitcoin. https://sbor.xyz

protocol_v4.name: Shadow Protocol
protocol_v4.bio: The v4 aggregator that leaves no trail. Best split across every pool, hooks included, sent to a fresh shadow. Routes for agents over x402.
texts: Four days, six more things live, and every one started with someone hitting a wall during a real swap: hooks that price by gas, a wallet reading a stale node, a balance that didn’t show. Now the router quotes at your real gas price, checks your wallet’s connection before you sign, and hands you a re

A swap can be fine on chain and still fail in your wallet, simply because the wallet is reading the chain through a node that fell behind. That’s why the router asks both before it lets you sign, and if your wallet is the problem, it fixes the connection for you. https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap CA:

No token list to wait for, no listing to request. Paste a contract address and the router works out where it actually trades and the best way to reach it. A fresh launch and a deep pool take the same three steps. $PV4

Every swap from your main wallet adds to a public history anyone can read. Shadow addresses give you fresh ones, rebuilt from one free signature every time you need them. No key file to lose, no database of yours on our servers.

Wrapping ETH was always a tax: an extra step, an extra approval, extra gas, and WETH left behind when something fails halfway. In v4 a pool can hold ETH itself, and when it does the router pays it in directly. Your ETH goes in, your token comes out.

A quote taken at zero gas price looks great and fails on chain, because some v4 hooks set their fee from the transaction’s own gas price. We learned that from a real reverted swap, and fixed it the same day: every quote, preflight and floor is now simulated at the base fee you’ll actually pay. https

Plenty of tokens launch with a deck and a “coming soon”. $PV4 launched with a router you can use right now, and it gets better every week from what people run into while using it. Open it, swap something small, judge for yourself.

A success screen is easy to fake. A block isn’t. When your swap lands, the router reads what actually hit your wallet and what the network charged, straight from the chain, and puts it next to the price you were quoted. Trust the receipt, not the app.

The safest money is money that never leaves your hands. There’s no Protocol V4 balance to top up and no vault to trust: your tokens leave your wallet, go through the pools, and come back to it, all inside one transaction you sign yourself. https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap

Doing a good swap by hand means knowing which pools exist, what each one keeps, whether the token is still on its curve, and how to cut your size between them, all before the price moves. We turned that whole afternoon into a quote you can read in five seconds.

Uniswap v4 spread liquidity across more pools than anyone can watch: every fee tier, every hook, every launch curve. You shouldn’t have to pick. Tell the router what you want and how much, it finds the pools and fills them all in the same transaction. $PV4

Update: swap receipts. A quote is a promise. A receipt is proof. After every swap, the router now reads the block it landed in and tells you what really reached your wallet, how that compares to what you were quoted, and what the gas cost you. And if your wallet doesn’t list the token yet, one click

Pools named, hooks named, fee per leg, minimum per leg, the block it was priced at, the link the moment it’s sent. If you like to know exactly what you signed, this router was built for you. $PV4 https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap
Every fix this week started as a reply under one of our posts. Keep them coming: tell us what confused you, what was slow, what didn’t work. We read all of it, and the router is better for it.

On this chain the network fee is so low that the trade itself is all that matters. Which is exactly why routing matters: the difference between a good and a bad route is worth far more than the gas you’ll ever pay here. https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap
Never used a v4 router? Bring a small amount, keep some ETH aside for gas, and read the route before you sign. The page checks the rest and won’t let you send a swap that would fail.

Comparing a quote to a chart is comparing a crowd to one person. The chart shows the last trade. Your quote shows what your exact size gets after it pushes through every pool on the route, fees and depth included. The router shows both, so you can see the gap before you sign.

The most common “the swap won’t go through” isn’t the swap. It’s an older transaction in your wallet, sent with too little gas, still sitting in the queue. Open your wallet’s activity, speed it up or cancel it, and everything behind it clears in seconds.

noctisdotxyz.bio: Private by default, provable on demand. TEE-powered AI agents with encrypted intents and view keys.

texts: Traditional finance has dark pools for a reason: when large orders are visible, the market moves against them. Onchain agents don’t have an equivalent yet. That’s the gap we’re building for.
Things NOCTIS will never ask you for: your seed phrase, a DM to “help” you buy, a “verification” transaction, or payment to join a whitelist. If someone asks, it isn’t us.
Most “AI agent” tokens are a chatbot with a wallet. The hard part isn’t the AI. It’s letting it act with real money safely, privately and within limits.
One of the hard parts we’re working through: running an LLM inside an enclave. Models are large, enclave memory is limited, and confidential GPUs cost more. We’ll share how we handle each one.
We’re designing NOCTIS as an execution layer, not another agent. Bring your own agent, any model or framework. We handle where it runs and how its trades settle.
Who NOCTIS is for: builders who don’t want their agent cloned the day it works, desks that don’t want to broadcast positions, and anyone letting an agent manage money without exposing their wallet.

What NOCTIS doesn’t hide: that a trade happened, enclave attestations, your policy hash, our contract code. What it does hide: your strategy, which trades are yours, your wallet, your exact rules. Private isn’t invisible.

What happens if someone tricks your agent with a malicious prompt or a fake data feed? On NOCTIS, the worst case is a rejected transaction. The contract checks where funds go and how much, whatever the agent says.
A sandwich attack, explained: a bot sees your buy, buys first, lets you buy at the higher price, then sells. Its profit is the extra you paid. It only works because your order was visible.
A human trader makes a few trades a day. An AI agent can trade all day, every day. Every trade is another clue about the strategy. Agents need privacy more than people do.
Honest question for anyone running a trading bot onchain: have you ever checked how easy it is to trace your bot’s wallet back to you?

texts: Same app, real privacy. Until this week Meryal's withdrawals were checked in the open. Now the contract only sees a Groth16 proof: no note, no index, no trace of the deposit it came from. Try it with a few dollars. https://www.meryalraven.sbs/spend

Two steps done this week, in the open, on chain. Next is the public part: a setup ceremony anyone can contribute to, and keeper seats for outside operators who bond $MERY and take a share of the key. https://www.meryalraven.sbs CA: 0x134e52ed8ee01cbb1fb714098b606c57366369fd

Your note never leaves your browser. Meryal's prover runs locally: snarkjs, the circuit's wasm and its key, served as plain files. It builds the witness from your seed and hands the relayer a proof and the public inputs, nothing else.

Update: No single key can read a Meryal position anymore. Sealed notes are encrypted to a key split in three. Two shares open a note, and the contract only accepts them near its liquidation price. Each keeper bonds $MERY. Deposits are approved on chain; only a multisig can refuse one.
Good morning team

Privacy only wins when it is the cheap default. On Meryal it already costs the user nothing extra: the proof takes two seconds in your browser, the relayer pays the gas, and the address that receives the money has never been seen before.

A public chain is a public diary. Every wallet you use can be read: what you hold, what you borrowed, where you spent it. Meryal breaks the thread between the position and the spending, with a proof instead of a promise. CA 0x134e52ed8Ee01Cbb1FB714098B606C57366369Fd

Need cash without selling your NVDA? Borrow against it at the Morpho market's rate. The USDG arrives as private notes, and you spend them from addresses nobody can tie to your position. Unaudited beta, small amounts. https://www.meryalraven.sbs/borrow

Tokenized stocks now have a five-year path to trade on chain. On chain, every position is readable: size, debt, liquidation price, and the wallet behind it. Meryal's sealed positions keep all of that behind a commitment, and prove on every step that the loan stays safe.

Shielded pools are turning into the privacy layer for payments. Meryal plugs a credit source into one: borrow against a stock token and the USDG lands in the pool as notes, withdrawn later by a zero-knowledge proof to any address. Shares in, private cash out.

Sealed positions are live on Meryal. Deposit NVDA, borrow USDG, repay, withdraw: each change is a proof made in your browser. The chain records a commitment and the amounts that moved, not whose position it is or how big it has grown.

Major Update live now : Meryal's privacy is now zero-knowledge. Withdrawals, credit activations and sealed positions are Groth16 proofs made in your browser in two seconds. A sealed position hides its size and debt, yet proves it stays solvent at every step. http://www.meryalraven.sbs/sealed CA: 0x1

Every credit line has an end date. After expiry and a grace hour anyone can close it, and what the agent did not spend goes back into the pool as the owner's note. The caller cannot send it anywhere else.

No IOU on Meryal is unsecured. When a line is reserved, the vault borrows its whole limit into escrow against the owner's stock. Every IOU is paid from that escrow, and the vault's liquidation rules keep the borrow solvent.

A finished session still holds dust. A one-time address holds a payment. Neither needs gas to clean up. The address signs once, the recycler deposits the rest into the pool, and the nonce fixes the note and the fee so a relayer can change neither.

x402 with a stealth extension. The agent signs a ReceiveWithAuthorization made out to Meryal's settler, with a nonce that commits to the one-time address. Whoever submits it, the USDG can only land there, announced once.

Agents paying agents means every agent is also a merchant. On Meryal a merchant publishes one meta-address. Each x402 payment to it lands at a new one-time address, settled by a contract that can only send it there. Revenue that is not a public line.

Every x402 payment is a public receipt: who paid whom, how much, when. Run an agent from one wallet and its whole shopping list is on chain. On Meryal each session pays from a fresh address, and a merchant with a meta-address is paid at a new one-time address every time.
Good morning

An agent never keeps the same address for long. A session lasts until it is spent, an hour old or 20 payments in, by default. Then the issuer derives the next one and moves on. Watch any one address and you see a short session, not the agent.

给审核模块接上事实源后，开始报一堆假阳性——本该核对数字的逻辑，把写法判据也当数字去核对，一堆「没出处」的误报。 我一开始以为是提示词不够精确，想着再加约束描述。 查到根因：facts和playbook被塞进了同一个数组返回。facts是带出处的数字事实，playbook是写法规则，压根没有数字可核对。结构长得一样，下游拿同一套逻辑处理，误判是必然的。 判据：校验语义不同的数据，哪怕字段结构一样，也别塞进同一个数组——下游只认结构，不认语义。 #系统设计
